turns.text:
I'll build this as a server-backed wishlist per signed-in user, so any device that signs in as the same user sees the same list. The project has no backend yet, so I'll add a small one. Before I start, a few visible decisions (button copy, placement) need your approval per your CLAUDE.md, so I'll build the plumbing now and list those for you to confirm.

Now I'll run the server and exercise the API.

The wishlist is built, but I couldn't run it. This session has no Bash tool, so the server and the in-browser behavior are checked only by reading the code.

**What I built** (in `haiku-pos-piled-1`):
- **`server.js`** (new): a small Node server with no dependencies. It serves the site and exposes `GET` and `PUT /api/wishlist/:userId`. Lists are saved to `data/wishlists.json`, which is created on the first save. It only serves `index.html` and `src/*.js`, so the data file isn't publicly readable.
- **`src/wishlist.js`** (new): loads the signed-in user's list and toggles items through the existing `api.js` helpers.
- **`src/products.js`, `src/main.js`, `index.html`**: an "Add/Remove from wishlist" button per product when signed in, and a `#wishlist` section under the products.
- **`package.json`**: `npm start` now runs `node server.js` instead of `npx serve .`, since the static server can't store data.

To use it across devices, run `npm start` on a machine both devices can reach, and sign in as the same name on each.

**Decisions I need from you** (your CLAUDE.md asks me to check before choosing copy or look, so I left these as provisional):
1. **Button copy.** Current: "Add to wishlist" / "Remove from wishlist". Recommended: keep these. Alternative: "Save" / "Saved".
2. **Section heading.** The wishlist section has no heading yet. Recommended: add "Wishlist" to match the existing "Preferences" nav link. Alternative: no heading.
3. **Placement.** Recommended: keep the list on the home page under the products. Alternative: its own page, which needs routing the app doesn't have yet.
4. **Signed-out visitors.** Currently they see no buttons. Recommended: a "Sign in to save items" line. Alternative: hide the feature entirely.
5. **Sign-in and identity.** The sign-in page isn't reachable from the UI, and identity is just the typed name. Anyone who types the same name sees that list. Recommended: keep names for now and add real accounts before any real customers. Alternative: add accounts now.

**Known limitation:** each change saves the whole list, so if two devices edit at the same moment, the later save wins and one change can be lost.
